questions.question: A regulated application must keep identical model behaviour until your team approves a change. What should you configure on the deployment?

options.text: Pin the model version and disable automatic upgrades
options.why: Correct. The deployment stays on the chosen version until you change it.
Temperature does not control versioning.

options.text: Enable upgrades to each new default
options.why: This changes behaviour without approval.
The deployment type does not pin the model version.

questions.explanation: Version pinning with no auto upgrade keeps behaviour stable.

questions.question: An app code uses the name of a model in each request, and a new model must replace it without code changes. What should the app call instead?

options.why: A key does not identify a model.
Correct. The deployment name is a stable handle, so the model behind it can change.
This ties code to one model.
This does not identify a model deployment.

questions.scenario: An agent in production begins giving poor answers after instructions were edited. Earlier versions were saved.
questions.question: What is the fastest safe fix?

options.why: Capacity affects throttling, not answer quality.

options.text: Delete the agent and recreate it
options.why: This loses history and takes longer than a rollback.

options.text: Switch the endpoint to the previous agent version
options.why: Correct. Versions are kept, so you can serve the earlier one immediately.
This removes protection and does not restore earlier behaviour.

questions.explanation: Each agent change creates a version that you can switch back to.

questions.question: Which setting of a model deployment determines how many tokens per minute it can process?

options.why: The version selects a model release, not throughput.
A guardrail controls content, not throughput.
A project is a workspace and has no effect on throughput.
Correct. Capacity is the slice of quota given to the deployment.

questions.explanation: Deployment capacity is taken from the quota for the model and deployment type.

questions.question: Which change to an agent creates a new agent version?

options.why: Correct. Any change to the model, instructions or tools creates a new version.
Reading data does not change the definition.
An evaluation scores the agent without changing it.
Viewing does not change the definition.
